newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares firmer, poised for new records.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares firmer, poised for new records.

text.p: Austrian shares closed slightly firmer on Thursday but below an all-time high reached in early trading, following strong international leads.
The ATX closed up 2.73 points or 0.22 percent at 1,250.36, below the historic high of 1,258,29. The previous all-time-high was at 1,257,96 points, reached on April 16, 1991.
Among the ATX constituents, 13 stocks were up while eight closed lower.
Traders said they expected a new attempt to break through resistance just below 1,258 points within the next few days.
"Volumes at the higher levels were disappointing", one trader said, adding that a brief period of consolidation may be in store before the ATX resumed its record run.
"If you hit new highs you always need fresh money but we failed the first time around," said another trader, adding that a new record may be reached as early as Friday.
Austrian-Italian insurer EA-Generali topped the day's decliners, falling 1.17 percent to 3,380 schillings after the group warned growth was likely to slow in the current year.
Fibre maker Lenzing led the gainers, rising 1.76 percent to 579 schillings.

In the banking sector, Creditanstalt preferred were up 0.98 percent at 464.50 while the bank's ordinary stock was down 0.27 percent at 743. Bank Austria, Creditanstalt's majority owner, earlier on Thursday said it was planning to merge both bank's investment banking activities.
Oil and chemical group OMV was up 1.13 percent at a new year-high of 1,430 schillings. Airport operator Flughafen Wien also hit a new high at 609.95 schillings, up nearly one percent.
The March ATX future was up 2.0 points at 1,252.0. -- Christian Gutlederer, Vienna newsroom +431 53112-275
